metadata.title: The Overlooked Growth Engine Powering Cisco Systems Stock

content.text:
You might think you know this networking giant, but a new business in AI infrastructure is quietly forging its next era of growth.
After a run that has seen Cisco Systems (CSCO) stock climb +46% in just three months, you might be wondering what could be left in the tank. The answer lies in a part of the business that is growing so fast, management's own forecasts can barely keep up.
A Large AI Order Book
Forget the Cisco of old. The company is rapidly becoming a critical supplier for the world's biggest AI players. In its most recent quarter, management revealed it now expects to take AI infrastructure orders of approximately $9 billion from hyperscalers in FY '26. To put that in perspective, just one quarter prior, the company was guiding for orders "in excess of $5 billion." This new forecast represents a substantial growth of "4.5x our FY '25 total." The demand is so strong that the company has already taken $5.3 billion in such orders year-to-date, with a full quarter still to go. This new demand represents a bonfire, not merely a flicker.
The Silicon Advantage
So, why are the biggest cloud providers suddenly turning to Cisco? Management points directly to its proprietary technology, particularly its systems and market-leading Acacia optics. The CEO has been clear: "If you don't have silicon, you're going to struggle to be relevant to the hyperscalers." The underlying chip design gives Cisco a significant differentiator and, crucially, "a lot more control over the supply chain." This allows the company to be more confident in its ability to deliver when competitors might be struggling with constraints. The strategy is clearly working, with the company landing 5 new design wins with hyperscalers in Q3 alone.
The Core Business Is Accelerating, Too
The natural question is whether this AI boom is masking weakness elsewhere. The evidence suggests the opposite. Even when you strip out the triple-digit growth from hyperscalers, Cisco's product orders were still up 19% year-over-year. That's an acceleration from the 10% growth seen in the prior quarter. This broad-based demand, with enterprise orders up 18% and public sector orders up 27%, pushes back against the idea that customers are simply pulling orders forward. The entire networking portfolio appears to be firing, with campus networking orders growing more than 25% as customers begin what Cisco sees as a "multiyear, multibillion-dollar" refresh cycle. We recently looked into the drivers behind this large AI bet and what it means for the company's valuation.
